key: And there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said: ‘It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he put to death the Gibeonites.’
s: A famine opens a chapter in which seven of Saul’s sons and grandsons are hanged at the Gibeonites’ demand; Metzudat David, on 21:1, reads the ‘bloody house’ as blood Saul shed unprotested by Israel, killing along with Nob’s priests the Gibeonites who served there.

evidence.gloss: [Metzudat David on ‘and for his bloody house’:] And for this, that the house of Saul was a house of blood, for he shed blood and Israel did not protest against him; and he goes on to explain what the blood he shed was, and said, because he put the Gibeonites to death: for when he killed the priests of Nob he killed then also the Gibeonites, who were there as hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of the LORD.

reason: Second judgement: the refuter is right on both counts and the entry can be put right. Key verse unchanged (verse.js ok; ref 2 Samuel 21:1, at [283,1]). PLAIN: day.js 21:6 and 21:8 give seven men of his sons, two Rizpah bore to Saul and five of Michal the daughter of Saul; the clause now says seven of Saul’s sons and grandsons, not seven sons. ATTRIBUTION: Radak on 21:1 relays Saadia Gaon’s answers (ending כך סידרם רבינו סעדיה גאון) and then what our Rabbis explained, choosing neither, so the three-year search is not his own reading; Radak is dropped. Metzudat David on the lemma ואל בית הדמים gives his own account in his own voice: Saul’s house is a house of blood because he shed blood and Israel did not protest, the blood being the Gibeonites killed with the priests of Nob, where they were hewers of wood and drawers of water. The sentence carries exactly that; it omits his further clause that Israel could not protest the priests’ killing, which it does not contradict. Rashi on the same verse reports two views (Yerushalmi and the Rabbis), so he was not preferred. Changed: by radak to metzudat-david, the reading, the plain-sense clause, and src. entry-check ok on the corrected entry.
